correctness.rationale: For all strictly positive rates and R0>1, the exact positive equilibrium yields q*=R0 and B=bγE=t e4/D with t=(R0−1)/R0 in (0,1). The characteristic polynomial calculated from J is λ4+e1 λ3+(e2+B)λ2+(e3+Bc)λ+BD. Expanding Δ3 gives base Hurwitz determinant e1e2e3−e3²−e1²e4>0, plus e1²(1−t)e4>0, B[c(e1e2−2e3)+e1e3]>0, and B²c(e1−c)>0; e1e2−3e3=∑_{i<j}αiαj(αi+αj)>0 and e1−c=α1+μL>0. All ηi positive, proving Hurwitz stability by the quartic Liénard–Chipart criterion. The proof excludes Hopf crossings of this equilibrium but not other global dynamics.
correctness.scope: Strictly positive stage transition, mortality, oviposition and capacity parameters; R0>1; uncontrolled four-stage continuous ODE; local spectral stability of unique positive equilibrium only.

No identified published result implies this universal assertion; best-of-knowledge with classical-stage-model priority risk.

value.rationale: The determinant condition in the motivating published four-stage mite model is not a mere arbitrary algebra exercise: it separates proven local coexistence stability from an entire unclassified positive-parameter region. Showing it is automatic gives a complete sharp qualitative local threshold picture and rules out Hopf loss of the positive equilibrium anywhere for R0>1, avoiding casewise quartic tests. The result is model-specific and elementary in technique, but closes a real model-level analytical gap; this is an independently useful stability conclusion.
risks: Model-specific, not a general four-stage feedback theorem.
